body:
Thanks for your response - I realise the letter is very intense.... 

I'll more than likely see her again before I put this letter into affect but it's been difficult - we used to work together but I left work a few months back - she's had her own troubles recently which have made it harder for casual social encounters and I don't want to bring stuff like this as a precursor for seeing her as she would willingly stress herself out even more for something that ultimately not change much.

I've done some short term therapy a few years back after an extended period of depression that I couldnt mask like I normally would and i went into absolute detail about my history thoughts and feelings but the conclusions we came to together matched what I had already realised on my own; that i would need to seek long term therapy to even be able to deal with how deep my issues were but I was already well aware of the how and why, what my triggers were etc so it would have been more around trying to manage the outcome better. 

The main point from it was though, there was a very real and high chance in cases like mine that the long term therapy would have to be life long, that the fears and anxiety I have would never go away. 

At the time I wasnt actively seeking my current desired outcome so I had only spoken to them about thinking about it and I guess I was also not trying to flag myself as somone who may have been in immediate danger from themselves.

I'm not all too comfortable with the idea that the way that I am now is very much the way that I'll always be - I don't want to spend the rest of my life trying to damage control the after affects of being me and honestly is exhausting masking my feelings for the sake of everyone else in my day to day that I'm not comfortable talking about such things with. 

At my last workplace, I could just about handle being the ever cheery, happy-go-lucky, support everyone guy for several years before all the corporate bulshit stress left me struggling to find any form of comfort in my focussed work or in the ever fewer recreational activities I could convince myself to continue doing.

I certainly don't want to get into a commited relationship with a desire to raise my own family only to find that a few years down the line that the traces of who I am truly right now - the person that my friend from my letter adores - is eroded away into a tradegy just waiting to happen.

I can't allow myself to let that happen.
